Known defects of the CVM publication

Source: vignettes/articles/data-defects.Rmd
data-defects.Rmd

This article is a referential inventory of known publication quirks of the CVM open-data feeds — heterogeneous identifier formats, declared-but-implicit unit scales, columns CVM ships under one name but indexes under another, tables published without a dictionary, and so on. cvmdata adopts a deliberate stance:

If it comes from CVM, it stays as in CVM, with only typographic normalization to snake_case lowercase. The package never invents content that CVM did not publish. Transformations exist only when CVM’s own metadata declares them (e.g. the ESCALA_MOEDA multiplier).

The result is a tibble that round-trips cleanly to the published source while still being analysis-ready. The table below catalogs the thirteen defects we have seen so far. The five structurally representative cases get a mini-example below; the others are single-paragraph references.

library(cvmdata)

Live chunks below use the default mirror backend (GitHub Releases + DuckDB): the docs build must not depend on the CVM portal being up — a portal timeout took the site down on 2026-06-03. The mirror releases follow the current mirror-<group>-<dataset>-latest naming since 2026-06-09, so the old live-portal pin is gone.

Inventory

# Defect Upstream behaviour cvmdata treatment
1 Embedded control characters in free-text FRE fields (e.g. BEL ) Experiencia_Profissional and similar carry raw control bytes Preserved verbatim — “stays as in CVM”. A cvm_strip_control_chars() helper is on the v0.2 list.
2 CEP loses leading zeros in CAD META declares tipo_dados: numeric; “01310-100” arrives as 1310100 Preserved; a cep_pad() helper is on the v0.2 list. The column is forced to character.
3 Empty Descrição / Domínio in some META FRE entries Reader sees partial metadata blocks Tolerated. The dictionary snapshot keeps the row with NA for the empty fields.
4 VL_CONTA declared decimal(29,10) Up to 29 digits of precision; R double resolves ~15–17 significant figures Documented limitation. No silent truncation; values above the safe range have not been observed in the public companies feed.
5 CD_CVM zero-padding inconsistent between datasets CAD ships 1023; ITR/DFP ship 001023 See example below. Preserved as published; cvm_fetch() filters by CNPJ, so the padding never enters a call.
6 CNPJ comes with punctuation (00.000.000/0001-91) Per-row formatting; not stripped upstream Preserved in cnpj_cia. cnpj accepts both punctuated and clean forms. cnpj_clean() / cnpj_format() round-trip.
7 VL_CONTA × ESCALA_MOEDA (UNIDADE / MIL / MILHÃO / BILHÃO) Two columns; user must multiply See example below. Applied via the canonical multiply_by_scale transformation; escala_moeda dropped.
8 Eight FRE tables ship without published META Dictionary .txt never released for empregado_PCD and seven kin See example below. YAML declares meta_status: missing; validate = "warn" or "skip" opt-in required.
9 ORDEM_EXERC ∈ {ÚLTIMO, PENÚLTIMO} per yearly CSV Each year’s CSV covers only the declared year and N − 1, and the N − 1 column is the issuer’s comparative, often restated Returned as-is by default. reading = c("original", "restated") reads an exercise by its own year and labels the figures originally filed and the comparative of the following year’s file. To assemble three or more consecutive years, pass an explicit year vector spanning the range.
10 FRE 2024 META URL anomalies Archive name is meta_fre_cia_aberta.zip (no _txt.zip suffix); empregado_local_faixa_etaria entry lives without the meta_ prefix Schema-level fixups: cvm_dictionary_url lists the archive plus entry; reader looks for both prefixed and bare entry names.
11 VERSAO per (cnpj_cia, dt_refer) enables re-filings Multiple rows for the same filing key when re-filed See example below. Applied via the canonical keep_latest_version transformation, which orders filings by delivery (see #14).
12 Dates as YYYY-MM-DD strings Plain strings in the CSV Converted to R Date for every column the dictionary declares tipo_dados: "date".
13 FRE-detail and some ITR/DFP tables lack a cd_cvm column Filter must run on CNPJ See example below. cvm_fetch() identifies issuers by CNPJ (or ticker) only, matching cnpj_cia or cnpj_companhia as the table carries.
14 Repeated filings and repeated rows Two filings under the same version; DFP/ITR statement CSVs repeat rows, often the whole statement See below. Detail tables keep the last delivery; submissao lists every one; identical rows dropped from DFP/ITR tables with cvmdata_warn_duplicate_filing.
15 A later filing delivered under a lower VERSAO The statement CSVs keep the highest version, not the last delivery See below. cvmdata_warn_stale_filing names the issuers; the table keeps the CVM numbers.
16 Comparative column filled with zeros When an issuer presents no comparative, the PENÚLTIMO rows carry 0, not NA: 21 banks did so for 2024 on the individual basis in the DFP 2025, after adopting CMN Resolution 4,966 without restating Returned as-is, including through reading = "restated". A zero in a comparative column of a bank’s individual statements for 2024 means “not presented”, not a zero balance.

Mini-examples for the structural cases

#5 — CD_CVM padding preserved per dataset

CAD ships CD_CVM unpadded, ITR/DFP pad to six digits. The same issuer, selected by CNPJ in both, shows the two forms:

a <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
               year = 2024, basis = "ind")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
b <- cvm_fetch("cad", "companhias", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
unique(a$cd_cvm)
#> [1] "001023"
unique(b$cd_cvm)
#> [1] "1023"

The returned cd_cvm column is whatever the dataset publishes — six-digit padded for DFP, two- to five-digit unpadded for CAD. Identifier columns are forced to character (CLAUDE.md §2.4) so neither form is corrupted. Because cvm_fetch() selects issuers by CNPJ, the padding never has to be normalised at the call; the registry is where a CVM code is translated to its CNPJ.

#7 — VL_CONTA × ESCALA_MOEDA applied as published

The published CSV has two columns: VL_CONTA (the raw figure) and ESCALA_MOEDA (one of UNIDADE, MIL, MILHÃO, BILHÃO). The schema declares the transformation, and the package returns absolute reais with escala_moeda dropped:

yaml::read_yaml(system.file(
  "extdata", "schemas", "dfp", "bpa.yaml", package = "cvmdata"
))$transformations
#> Warning in file(file, "rt", encoding = fileEncoding): file("") only supports
#> open = "w+" and open = "w+b": using the former

#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

bpa[bpa$cd_conta == "1" & bpa$ordem_exerc == "ÚLTIMO", "vl_conta"]

#8 — META missing in 8 FRE tables, opt-in via validate

The eight workforce-diversity tables in FRE (empregado_PCD, empregado_local_declaracao_genero, etc.) ship without a CVM dictionary. The default validate = "strict" refuses to read them:

cvm_fetch("fre", "empregado_PCD",
          cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", year = 2024)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> ℹ source: "mirror" | fetched_at: 2026-10-24 10:16:25.195564
#> ℹ group: "companhias" | dataset: "fre" | table: "empregado_PCD"
#> # A tibble: 0 × 11
#> # ℹ 11 variables: cnpj_companhia <chr>, data_referencia <date>, versao <chr>,
#> #   id_documento <chr>, nome_companhia <chr>, codigo_posicao <chr>,
#> #   posicao <chr>, quantidade_pcd <dbl>, quantidade_nao_pcd <dbl>,
#> #   quantidade_sem_resposta <dbl>, year <int>

validate = "warn" returns the data and emits cvmdata_warn_meta_unavailable; "skip" silences the warning. cvm_dictionary() for these tables returns NA in every metadata column except campo / campo_original — the package never invents content CVM did not publish.

See the fre article for the worked example.

#11 — keep_latest_version collapses re-filings

A filing can be re-submitted; CVM keeps every version in the CSV. For each detail table where re-filings happen, the schema declares a keep_latest_version transformation which the package applies before returning:

yaml::read_yaml(system.file(
  "extdata", "schemas", "fre", "auditor.yaml", package = "cvmdata"
))$transformations
#> Warning in file(file, "rt", encoding = fileEncoding): file("") only supports
#> open = "w+" and open = "w+b": using the former
#> NULL

Result: at most one row per filing key in the returned tibble. The submissao table of each dataset is the exception: it is the filing index and returns every delivery, with its receipt date and document id (see #14 and #15 below for how to read the current one).

auditor <- cvm_fetch("fre", "auditor",
                     cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", year = 2024)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
# One row per (cnpj_companhia, data_referencia):
nrow(unique(auditor[, c("cnpj_companhia", "data_referencia")])) ==
  nrow(auditor)
#> [1] FALSE

#13 — Tables without cd_cvm

fre/auditor, dfp/composicao_capital, dfp/parecer, and several FRE-detail tables index by cnpj_companhia (or cnpj_cia) without carrying cd_cvm. cvm_fetch() identifies issuers by CNPJ (or by a B3 ticker, resolved to CNPJ), and matches whichever CNPJ column the table carries:

auditor <- cvm_fetch("fre", "auditor",
                     cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", year = 2024)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpLsd3vV/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
"cd_cvm" %in% names(auditor)
#> [1] FALSE
unique(auditor$cnpj_companhia)
#> [1] "00.000.000/0001-91"
unique(auditor$nome_companhia)
#> [1] "BCO BRASIL S.A."

The interface is identical regardless of which table holds CD_CVM natively. A CVM code known only by itself is translated to its CNPJ through the registry (cvm_fetch("cad", "companhias")) or the dataset’s submissao; the deprecated issuer_fetch() still does that lookup on the caller’s behalf until it is removed.

#14 and #15 — VERSAO is not a filing key

keep_latest_version ranks filings by delivery, not by version number: receipt date (dt_receb, data_entrega), then the CVM document id, then versao. Tables without delivery columns fall back to the highest versao. Two cases measured on 2026-10-18 show why the version number alone fails:

  • TRV XLIII Securitizadora, DFP 2023. The filing index lists two deliveries as version 1 (document ids 135158 and 135670). The DFP statement CSVs carry both, every account twice, with no column to tell them apart, so a sum over the issuer counts double. Dibens Leasing (ITR, 2023-09-30) is the same case.

    Repeated rows are more common than repeated filings. Across every DFP and ITR file from 2010 to 2026, 884 issuer-period-table cases have the whole statement doubled and 110 more a few accounts repeated, most of them with a single filing in the index (AXIA Energia Norte, DFP 2023, is one). A statement has one row per account, order and period, so the package drops the identical copies and warns with cvmdata_warn_duplicate_filing. Copies that differ in vl_conta are kept, with cvmdata_warn_conflicting_filing, since nothing says which is right.

  • Travessia Securitizadora VI, DFP 2024. Versions 1, 2 and again 1, the last one delivered on 2025-08-14. That filing has other numbers (total assets R$ 14.4 million against R$ 31.2 million in version 2), and it is the one the issuer reports as the 2024 comparative in its DFP 2025. The DFP 2024 statement CSVs still hold version 2. The package returns the CVM numbers and warns with cvmdata_warn_stale_filing.

Both checks read the dataset’s submissao of the same year, take the last delivery of each filing key from it, and run for either backend. options(cvmdata.check_filings = FALSE) turns them off.

The submissao itself is not collapsed since 0.2.0.9000: it lists every delivery of a filing, so the history behind both cases above is one call away, and the current filing is the last row by receipt date, then document id, then versao:

history <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "submissao",
                     cnpj = "43.335.774/0001-86", year = 2024)
history[, c("dt_refer", "versao", "id_doc", "dt_receb")]
# Three deliveries for 2024-12-31: versions 1, 2 and again 1.

current <- history |>
  dplyr::arrange(dt_receb, as.integer(id_doc), as.integer(versao)) |>
  dplyr::slice_tail(n = 1, by = c(cnpj_cia, dt_refer))
# id_doc and versao are character (identifiers); as.integer() orders
# them numerically.

Before this release the index returned only that last row, so a join of submissao to a statement table on (cnpj_cia, dt_refer) matched one delivery; it now matches all of them, and the recipe above restores the one-row-per-filing view.

Reading the other defects directly

For defects 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 10, and 12 the package’s behaviour is either purely preservational (1, 2, 3, 4, 6) or structurally declared in the schema (9, 10, 12). The inventory table above points at each YAML and at the relevant CLAUDE.md section; the package’s source under R/transform-schema.R, R/util-csv-cvm.R, R/api-cvm-fetch.R and R/api-issuer-fetch.R is the canonical reference.
